look_here_first: FIRST find a MIDDLE STEM LEAF still attached to an opposite leaf node: each leaf is SIMPLE (one lance-shaped blade), sessile or nearly so, often toothed, rather than three separate leaflets attached to a common leafstalk (B. frondosa). SECOND inspect head: usually 7–8 showy yellow rays about 15–25 mm long and 5–7+ OUTER CALYCULUS green leaflike bractlets, then the INNER overlapping phyllaries. THIRD compare mature fruit with B. cernua: B. laevis outer cypselae 6–8 mm, inner 8–10 mm, margins NOT conspicuously thickened or corky-winged, usually 2–4 barbed awns 3–5 mm long; B. cernua fruits have more conspicuous thickened/winged margins, often shorter awns and smaller rays. Both can have nodding ripe heads. Flower color, 'nodding' or wetland site alone are not enough.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: ANNUAL herb, SOMETIMES PERSISTING, about 20–60(-120+) cm in FNA; most frequent in marshy margins, wet meadows, pools and streams. Older project label 'perennial wetland' was too absolute and scientifically corrected.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite (occasionally 3–4 at a node), SIMPLE sessile (without individual leaflet stalks); blades linear to lanceolate or elliptic/obovate, 20–160+ mm, coarse teeth common; examine actual attachment on the stem.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Usually 7–8 rays about 15–25(-30) mm, but rays occasionally absent. Two concentric bract zones below head: OUTER calyculus often 5–7(-9+) green leaflike bractlets around 10–12 mm, INNER involucre of 8–12 phyllaries about 6–8 mm. May nod in fruit; cannot use head nodding alone vs B. cernua.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Mature outer cypselae approximately 6–8 mm and inner approximately 8–10 mm, with non-corky (not conspicuously winged) margins and 2–4 retrorsely barbed pappus awns about 3–5 mm; check fruit at 10× versus B. cernua's often corky/thickened fruit margins.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Opposite whole SIMPLE stem leaves, one toothed blade attached at each leaf base; cannot confuse with three compound leaflets.; Showy head commonly 7–8 rays, each typically around 15–25 mm (but rays occasionally reduced or absent).; OUTER calyculus of ~5–7 green leaflike bractlets surrounding INNER ring of ~8–12 overlapping phyllaries; show separate colored labels.; Mature cypselae OUTER 6–8 vs INNER 8–10 mm, 2–4 awns 3–5 mm; photo of true fruit required, not generic beggartick.; Versus B. cernua: cernua generally shorter rays (often 2–15 mm) and outer fruits with thickened/corky or winged margins; overlaps exist.; FNA: ANNUAL SOMETIMES PERSISTING; do not describe as invariably perennial.; October flowering is often expected in suitable wetland habitat, but plant/fruit state varies with site.

lookalikes.differences: Frondosa bears usually 3 (occasionally 5) leaflets and generally lacks showy rays, whereas laevis has one simple sessile blade per leaf and often showy rays. Cernua also simple-leaved; separate by longer usual ray lamina (laevis 15–25 mm vs cernua 2–15 mm), non-corky cypsela margins and 3–5 mm awns versus cernua's often distinctly thickened/winged margins and 1–4 mm awns. FNA explicitly warns of phenotypic overlap; keep Bidens cf. laevis if uncertain.
